problem.headline:
You answer for care
you cannot verify
problem.sub: The county carries the liability. The vendor holds the data. Most of the help on offer leaves that gap exactly where it is.

items.title: Vendors grading their own work
items.text: Your compliance picture comes from the company you pay, measured with its own data and its own definitions.

items.title: Consultants who do not know jails
items.text: Generalist healthcare advisors miss how custody operations and correctional standards shape every clinical decision.

items.title: Reports that sit on a shelf
items.text: You pay for a thick assessment, then nothing changes because no one owns the corrective actions.

items.title: Compliance tracked in spreadsheets
items.text: Staff rebuild the same metrics by hand every month, and nobody fully trusts the numbers.

items.title: Surprises you hear about last
items.text: A survey finding, an in-custody death review or a lawsuit shows you the gap when it is too late to close it.

about.headline:
Where accountability meets action
in correctional healthcare
body: People in custody are owed constitutional-level care, and the agencies responsible for them need an objective way to know whether they are getting it. Actura Health exists to provide that.

We are the independent layer between the jail or prison and its healthcare vendor. We do not deliver medical care, so we never audit a competitor or ourselves. We bring NCCHC-level clinical expertise together with health system operations and EHR experience, with particular depth in California: Title 15 and CalAIM Justice-Involved.
